chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Qasim ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Musa ibn Zanjawiya al-Tafleysi, from Abu Umar al-Hannat, from Ismail al-Sayqal al-Razi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and with me were two garments. He said to me: 'O Abu Ismail! Many garments come to me from your side, but these two garments that you are carrying do not come to me like them.' I said: 'May I be your ransom, the mother of Ismail spun them, and I wove them.' He said to me: 'A weaver?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do not be a weaver.' I said: 'Then what should I be?' He said: 'Be a polisher.' And there were two hundred dirhams with me, so I bought swords and old mirrors with them, and I arrived in Rayy with them, and I sold them for a great profit.
ai.seo_question: What profession did Imam al-Sadiq recommend to Ismail al-Sayqal and why?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s practical wisdom in guiding Ismail al-Sayqal to leverage his specific skill of weaving to produce high-quality goods for trade, rather than merely performing the labor of weaving itself. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on professional specialization and commercial acumen, illustrating how mastering a craft can lead to financial success and social mobility within the early Islamic community.
